Subject: Next steps: Private VPC deployment & network questions

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re all aligned:

Summary of requirements we heard:
- Preferred deployment: Private VPC (FinLytics wants network isolation and on-prem connectivity).
- Unsure on exact networking approach: VPC Peering vs AWS PrivateLink — you said you’d like to evaluate both.
- IP allowlist needed for a handful of on-prem management hosts and CI runners (~5 IPs to start).
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required; you need evidence of audit logs and key management options.
- Throughput estimate: ~300 RPS peak for inference (text-gen) with spiky bursts; initial pilot smaller.
- Timeline: pilot environment within 3-4 weeks, production in ~8-10 weeks (contingent on procurement and network setup).

Action items (proposed):
1) Alex: share AWS account ID for peering/privatelink testing + network contact.
2) Sean/Marissa: send VPC checklist and MxA (attached) and propose follow-up for SRE deep dive.
3) Dev: share compliance/SOC2 artifacts and KMS options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan.pdf (MMP with milestones & proposed SOW).

Can you confirm the AWS account ID and preferred follow-up times? I’ll loop in Marissa to take the network deep-dive.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher

Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Private VPC deployment & network questions

Appreciate the quick reply, Alex — added Lisa (hi Lisa).

Short answers to your questions:
- PrivateLink vs Peering: both supported. For the pilot we typically recommend VPC Peering (faster to set up). For production, PrivateLink + interface endpoints is preferred for tighter security and no route table changes on your side.
- Allowlist: we can accept individual IPv4 addresses (preferred), but we also support CIDR blocks if you need to open ranges.
- Egress: Redwood does not require a NAT Gateway inside your VPC for our peering setup. If you use PrivateLink, outbound from our worker infra is through our managed VPC and we can limit egress; we’ll document exact external endpoints needed.

Marissa — can you take the network deep-dive with Lisa and provide the checklist/file we use for peering vs PrivateLink? Dev, please share the SOC2 artifact link and KMS options (customer-managed KMS vs Redwood-managed).

Proposed follow-up slots (PST):
- Mon 10/18 09:00-09:30
- Mon 10/18 11:00-11:30

If those don’t work, toss a few times and we’ll accommodate.

Sean

Hi Lisa / Alex — nice to e-meet you. I’ll run the VPC/network checklist and we can use the call to walk through details. Attached is a lightweight template we use to capture required values.

Quick checklist highlights (please confirm):
- AWS Account ID: 987654321000 (confirmed)
- Preferred option for production: AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) — we’ll document endpoints and PKI/certs for TLS.
- For pilot: VPC Peering is acceptable and typically faster to stand up. We need peering CIDRs and route table access for the peer.
- IP allowlist: we accept individual public IPv4 addresses. Please provide the list for the management hosts and CI runners.
- Ports: primarily 443 for HTTPS. If you plan to use metrics forwarding or health checks over custom ports, list them now.
- Route propagation: not required for peering; please do not enable automatic propagation unless you want routes inserted into our route tables.

Please attach or paste: VPC CIDRs for the peer, route table IDs, and the first set of allowlist IPs. I’ve attached vpc-configuration-template.yaml for your convenience.

Proposed meeting confirmation: Mon 10/18 11:00-11:30 PST works for me.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
